newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel oil offers rise, buyers quiet.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel oil offers rise, buyers quiet.

text.p: European straight-run fuel oil offer levels rose on Friday but buyers stepped back, wary of buying too far forward with crude volatile, traders said.
Offers of $108 and $109 were heard, but few buyers were prepared to take them seriously for now. Notional dealing prices were around $104-$107 a tonne fob.
"If someone had to buy now they would have to pay $107-$108 but if you can wait you should do better in a flat market," said one trader.
The amount of Russian straight-run available was disputed earlier in the day. But by close of business most agreed supply was tight and prices firm.
One E-4 of uncertain quality was believed on offer from Klaipeda at around three means plus $3-$4. Most Ventspils and Tuapse material was going on term contracts with little offered spot.
Supplies out of St. Petersburg were still thin, with technical problems blamed for delays in river-borne material. Just one cargo went this week, with one more due next week.
